Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing + SLA rebate structure

Hi Laura / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. BlueNexus is actively sizing an LLM-hosted tier and we need to understand two things from Redwood before we can finalize our internal budgeting and procurement timelines: a) a baseline hosted API rate card for monthly consumption bands up to ~30B tokens, and b) the structure you propose for SLA rebates/credits tied to sustained latency/availability misses — specifically how rebates scale with committed throughput and how burst usage is treated.

Our procurement window is tight (need numbers by 10/27). A few specifics that would help:
- Baseline per-token price for hosted generation (no embeddings) at 0-5B, 5-15B, 15-30B monthly buckets
- Any step/volume discounts for multi-month commitments (3/6/12 months) and whether unused committed tokens convert to credits
- How you calculate SLA rebates (per-hour vs monthly cap), thresholds for latency (p99) and availability, and whether rebates are explicit dollar credits or percentage discounts applied to the following invoice
- Treatment of burst traffic above commit: flat overage price vs blended smoothing; are there protective collars so our effective unit cost doesn't spike during rare surges?

We've attached a short usage snapshot and some expected seasonality. If you can send a draft rate card and an SLA addendum we can circulate internally. Happy to hop on a 30-min call — is 10/22 or 10/26 morning PT possible?

Thanks,
Evan Park
VP, Platform Partnerships
BlueNexus Technologies

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@bluenexus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing + SLA rebate structure

Hi Evan — appreciate the clarity and the timeline.

High-level answers up front, then I attached a starter spreadsheet (SLA_Rebate_Tiers_v2.xlsx) with worked examples so your finance team can eyeball the numbers quickly:

- Baseline hosted generation: we recommend starting with a 3-band structure. Nominal list is: 0-5B = $0.0009/token, 5-15B = $0.0007/token, 15-30B = $0.00055/token. Those are baseline list; negotiated commits can move you lower.
- Multi-month commitments: standard discounts are additive on top of bands: 3mo = 5% off list, 6mo = 9% off, 12mo = 14% off. Commit credits are consumed first; unused committed tokens convert to account credits valid for 12 months (not refundable).
- SLA rebate mechanics: we propose a tiered credit schedule tied to monthly p99 latency and monthly uptime. Example from attached: p99 > target but < x => 5% invoice credit; p99 >= x => 15% credit; availability < 99.5% => incremental credits up to a 30% monthly cap. Credits are applied as invoice line item credits the following billing cycle.
- Burst treatment: we offer a blended smoothing option for burst months which averages your monthly unit cost over a 90-day rolling window (protects from spikes), or a flat overage at 2x baseline unit price. The blended option requires a modest committed buffer and is recommended for unpredictable burst patterns.

If that direction sounds promising, I can schedule a 30-min call with Ben and our finance lead to run a quick simulation against your numbers. I have availability 10/26 10:00-11:30 PT or 10/27 08:30-10:00 PT.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Rebate_Tiers_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 47 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@bluenexus.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing + SLA rebate structure

Evan — looping in some math and two model scenarios so you can see the dollar impact. See attached (revenue-impact-sim.csv). Quick notes:

- Example A (steady state): 12mo commit at midpoint of 10B tokens/month using 6mo discount curve results in an effective unit price ~ $0.00063/token after commit and a 1.5% backlog credit allowance.
- Example B (spiky): monthly variance with 3 high-burst months — with the blended smoothing option your 90-day effective price smooths to ~$0.00071/token; with overage pricing raw spikes can reach $0.0014/token for the high months.

SLA rebate calculation detail (from our finance ops): credits calculated pro-rata against the monthly consumption charge; if multiple SLA conditions trigger we apply credits sequentially but cap total credits to 30% of the monthly invoice (we can discuss raising cap for higher-commit customers).

A few questions back to you so we can nail a proposal:
1) Do you need rebates to be cash refunds (we typically do credits) for your accounting?
2) Is there a preferred term (3/6/12) you want modeled?
3) Any regional constraints — are tokens primarily US-region or split with EU? (affects routing & pricing)

If you want a formal redline we can draft an SLA addendum for signature — Laura / I can take that to legal.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: revenue-impact-sim.csv (simulation, 9 KB)
